phenotype_specificity.statement: Cohort-level only. The paper gives no clinical features per person; each Table 1 row gives only the LAD-I expression type. No testing of other genes is reported.

quotes.quote: Characteristic features are delayed separation of the umbilical cord and strong leukocytosis, especially neutrophilia, during periods of infection.
The patients suffer from recurrent, life-threatening bacterial and fungal infections and from impaired wound healing.

In this nomenclature the superscript symbol indicates whether the protein is present at < 5% of normal expression (^o), diminished in expression (^−), i.e. between 5% and 20% of normal expression, or normally present but nonfunctional (^+)

Where possible we have cross-referenced the mutations indicated in the present article with those in an LAD-I, LAD-II and LAD-III database that lists these patients by accession number.

functional.statement: Table 1 gives CD18 normally present but nonfunctional (LAD-I^+) for this variant row. The paper says the type is based mainly on flow cytometry of the patients' leukocytes (patient cells), sometimes on COS-cell co-transfection; it does not say which applies to this row, and gives no values or controls. 42625796 reports, citing Mathew et al. (ref [43] in 22134107), that a p.Asp231His patient had normal surface LFA-1, Mac-1 and p150,95 but complete loss of adhesion to physiological ligands (patient cells, second-hand; the Mathew paper is not in this batch).

This information is based on immune reactivity of the patients’ leukocytes with monoclonal antibodies analyzed by flow cytometry and sometimes on similar analyses of COS cells cotransfected with mutant CD18 molecules and wild-type CD11 molecules.

Mathew et al. described a compound heterozygous LAD I patient harboring a p.Asp231His mutation, located in close proximity to p.Glu234, who exhibited normal surface expression of LFA-1, Mac-1, and p150,95, but a complete loss of adhesion to physiological ligands (15).

[43] Mathew EC, Shaw JM, Bonilla FA, et al, 2000, A novel point mutation in CD18 causing the expression of dysfunctional CD11/CD18 leucocyte integrins in a patient with leucocyte adhesion deficiency, Clin. Exp. Immunol PMID:10886250
In a number of cases functionality of the mutant CD18 proteins was tested in cellular adherence assays to β_2 ligands.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Missense variant, p.(Asp231His), from the batch HGVS. 22134107 says most point mutations lie in the conserved betaI domain (exons 5-9); 42625796 places Asp231 close to Glu234 in the betaI-like domain. The paper describes LAD-I as autosomal recessive and caused by decreased expression or function of CD18 (beta-2 integrin).

quotes.quote: Leukocyte adhesion deficiency (LAD) is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by decreased expression or functioning of CD18, the β_2 subunit of the leukocyte β_2 integrins [1].
Usually, this leads to the absence or decreased expression of the β_2 integrins on the leukocyte surface, but sometimes a normal expression of nonfunctional β_2 integrins is found.
Most of the point mutations are found in a ~240-residue domain that is highly conserved in all β integrin subunits and coded for by exons 5 – 9 of ITGB2 (figure 1).

Mathew et al. described a compound heterozygous LAD I patient harboring a p.Asp231His mutation, located in close proximity to p.Glu234, who exhibited normal surface expression of LFA-1, Mac-1, and p150,95, but a complete loss of adhesion to physiological ligands (15).

authors_classification.statement: No formal classification. The authors list the variant in Table 1 'Mutations in the LAD-I gene ITGB2', separate from the polymorphisms of Table 2.

concerns: 22134107 is a mutation-database update: the variant appears only as a Table 1 row with an accession number, with no case description, sex, clinical phenotype, zygosity or parental testing.
Same person as in G-lad1-046: accession A0075 (identity LAD1-ID0388) is also listed under c.755G>A (p.Trp252X), typed LAD-I^o there but LAD-I^+ here.
Accession A0013 is also listed under c.850G>A (p.Gly284Ser), typed LAD-I^o there but LAD-I^+ here. The table gives type per variant row, so each person's own CD18 level is unclear.
The c.850G>A row carries footnote c ('And reverse mutations in a small subset of lymphocytes [32]'), i.e. revertant changes reported for some carriers of that allele; not checked for A0013.
The A0013 report is probably ref [43] (Mathew 2000), the paper 42625796 cites for p.Asp231His; that link is an inference from the citations, not stated.
22134107 numbers cDNA from the A of the ATG (+1), which matches the batch numbering; it names no RefSeq transcript (it mentions GenBank M15395 only for the offset).
notes_for_panel: Typed LAD-I^+ (normal expression but nonfunctional). The only functional description is second-hand, in 42625796.
